title: Crypto Brief — 25 Nov 2026
intro: European trading hours open under persistent risk-off pressure as a deepening global tech rout and mounting AI debt worries weigh heavily on broader financial markets. The U.S. dollar index gains ground at 104.07 alongside falling Treasury yields at 4.904% as investors brace for critical macroeconomic data releases.

sections.heading: Crypto theme
sections.content: Risk appetite remains severely constrained as the broader equities sell-off, highlighted by a 1.99 percent drop in the Nasdaq 100, spills directly into digital asset flows. Macroeconomic anxiety dominates sentiment ahead of this afternoon's crucial U.S. Core PCE Price Index and Prelim GDP figures.

sections.heading: Bitcoin & Ether
sections.content: Bitcoin trades down 1.57 percent at 58,811 under ongoing downside pressure while Ethereum lower by 2.47 percent holds an ETH/BTC ratio of 0.02782 at 1,636.20. Both major assets maintain a fragile structure as they test lower boundaries amid the broader market downturn.

sections.heading: Altcoins
sections.content: Alternative assets lag the broader market with 5 of 10 tracked alts beating Bitcoin over the past week, led by Litecoin gaining 1.2 percent while Zcash leads weekly losses down 7.2 percent.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▲ Bullish · Bitcoin — above 59,190 opens 61,200 · invalid below 58,200*
A relief bounce driven by cooler than expected U.S. Core PCE inflation data relieving macroeconomic pressure.
- *▼ Bearish · Ethereum — below 1,620.00 opens 1,550.00 · invalid above 1,655.00*
Continued downside momentum fueled by deepening tech sector liquidations and risk aversion.
- *▼ Bearish · Solana — below 66.00 opens 63.50 · invalid above 68.50*
Accelerated outflows following broader altcoin weakness and persistent pressure on layer-one valuations.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Hotter than expected U.S. PCE inflation figures triggering further macro tightening fears.
- Intensification of the global tech rout spilling over into risk asset liquidations.
